aggregate_emails v3 - Rate Sanity Report

Entity-level EDA - generated 2026-04-24T16:19:42Z

Abstract. aggregate_emails v3 covers 4,575 emails spanning 2021-08 through 2026-04. 2,274 emails (49.7%) fall in the VO-tracking era (>= 2024-03-01). Headline medians: open 30.8%, VO 17.5%, click 9.3%, action 5.1%, click-per-open 30.7%, action-per-click 82.0%. Verdict: Flag: action_rate, action_per_click median(s) outside expected bands - see section 4.

1. Introduction

This report answers one question: are the per-email rates in aggregate_emails v3 plausible for advocacy email? It does NOT re-examine field-level quality (null rates, range flags, embedding coverage) - those were covered in projects/civic_shout_actions_routing/eda/aggregate-emails-quality.md (commit 3ef5200). Instead, it treats the six derived rates as the primary subject: open rate, verified-open rate, click rate, action rate, click-per-open, and action-per-click.

v3 upgrades the engagement counters (total_*) to a 24-month attribution window (vs. ~1 month in v1/v2), making rates higher than v1/v2. All rate computations use denominator guards that null out rates where the denominator is zero or null.

4. Rate Sanity Invariants

Hard invariants are treated as bugs if violated. Report-only incidence counts are diagnostic - legitimate data patterns that are worth noting but do not indicate bad data.

CheckTypeViolation countNotes
total_vo <= total_opensHARD INVARIANT115Expected ~115 (MPP dedup artifact per prior EDA R2)
total_clicks > total_opensREPORT-ONLY (incidence)79Legitimate - images-disabled clicks fire without open pixel
total_actions > total_sentREPORT-ONLY (incidence)0Legitimate - total_sent is unique users; total_actions is row count
open_rate <= 100%HARD INVARIANT0PASS
vo_rate <= 100%HARD INVARIANT0PASS
click_rate <= 100%HARD INVARIANT0PASS
click_per_open <= 100%HARD INVARIANT76FAIL (76 emails)
action_rate > 100%REPORT-ONLY tail (not a bug)0Attribution semantics allow >100%; inspect distribution tail
action_per_click > 100%REPORT-ONLY tail (not a bug)647Attribution semantics allow >100%; inspect distribution tail

Chart C shows a pass/fail breakdown for each check. Green = passing rows; red = violations or incidence.

5. Temporal Stability

Chart D shows the monthly median of each rate over time. The red-shaded region covers pre-VO-era (before 2024-03-01) ; the green band is the expected advocacy range.

Chart E shows rate vs. total_sent as a hexbin plot (log-x). High variance at low send volumes confirms that raw rates are noisy for small sends and motivates a minimum-denominator gate or Bayesian smoothing.

6. Funnel shape by volume quartile

Chart F normalizes every email to fraction of total_sent so the funnel shape (opens → VO → clicks → actions) is comparable across sends of any size. Panels split emails by send-volume quartile (recomputed on emails with total_sent >= 100). The blue line is the quartile median profile with P10-P90 shaded. Red lines are the three emails in each quartile with the most-unusual rate profile vs their peers. A break in a line on the VO stage indicates a pre-VO-era email.

How unusual is unusual? |z-score| distribution per rate

Chart G shows the empirical distribution of absolute z-scores (within each email's volume quartile cohort) for the four base rates. Most emails are within |z|<2 of their quartile median; tails beyond |z|=3 are the drivers that push specific emails to the top of the unusualness table below.

Most-unusual emails per volume quartile

Unusualness = sum of |z-score| across the 4 rates, vs. the email's quartile cohort. Null rates contribute 0. The bolded z-score is the driver — the rate pulling this email away from its peers the hardest. Inspect these before trusting rate features on the full corpus.

7. Next Steps

  1. Choose a send-volume gate. Chart E shows variance inflation below ~500 sends. The minimum-denominator thresholds in this report (>= 100 sent for open/vo/click/action rates) are a starting point; a smoothed (Empirical Bayes) rate may be more powerful for small sends. Owner: next investigation that builds rate-based features.
  2. Investigate any out-of-band medians. Review the distribution tail and confirm the outlier emails are not data errors (test sends, seed accounts, etc.). Owner: EDA follow-up.
  3. Confirm VO-era stability. Chart D shows whether vo_rate stabilised after 2024-03. If trending up, restrict analyses to a stable sub-window. Owner: next investigation using VO signal.
  4. Decide on leaky-column exclusion policy. The prior EDA flagged sent_in_range / opens_in_range / clicks_in_range as misleading (R5). Do not include these flags in modeling matrices without a design decision on what 'in range' means post-v3.

Expected advocacy-email bands (industry norms)

The bands are opinionated estimates from industry benchmarks. If a median falls outside its band, the flag means 'worth understanding why', NOT 'data is broken'.

Open questions carried from prior EDA

  • Leaky-column exclusion policy: sent_in_range, opens_in_range, clicks_in_range are known to be misleading (prior EDA R5). Deferred.
  • Bayesian smoothing prior choice: which Beta prior parameters suit Civic Shout? Not answered here.
  • VO-era hard filter vs. null-handling: downstream features may hard-filter to VO-era rows or treat pre-era rows as a separate regime. This report uses null-gating.
